case_title.quote: NARENDER SINGH & ORS. v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH

number_of_accused.correct_value: 7 accused in total; 5 appellants (A2 to A6)
number_of_accused.quote: Out of 7 accused, A2 toA6 are the appellants before us
number_of_accused.reason: Five are appellants, but the judgment says there were seven accused (one juvenile separated, A1 not appealing).

accused_gender.quote: A5 while abusing the deceased and making a pronouncement that he cannot escape
accused_gender.reason: Accused are referred to as male; reasonable inference.

accused_age.reason: Ages are not given; only that one accused was a juvenile.

accused_caste.reason: Caste not stated; only 'same community' is mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: Ram Bhuvan, son of Sunder Lal Sharma

accused_victim_relationship.reason: No relationship is stated beyond alleged enmity.

offence_category.quote: convicted the appellants accused for the offence under Section 302

weapon.quote: A5 was holding a sword, A6 was holding a Farsa, A2 was having an axe while A 1, A3 and A4 were having lathis

confession.quote: Section 27 Statement under Exhibits P18 to P21
confession.reason: Section 27 statements are only referred to.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: 8 injuries were noted... injury Nos. 4,5, 6 and7 were noted as grievous

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted the appellants accused for the offence under Section 302 read with Sections 148 and 149 IPC

high_court_outcome.quote: The Division Bench having confirmed the conviction and sentence

offence_finally_established.quote: the involvement of the appellants was, therefore, fully established
offence_finally_established.reason: Murder under s.302 with ss.148/149 upheld.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Victim was sitting with P.W.3, P.W.6 and Rangnath Sharma (three men), not two.
neutral_facts.quote: P.W.3, 6 and the deceased were sitting and conversing with each other along with one Rangnath Sharma
neutral_facts.reason: Says victim was with 'two men'; judgment names three companions. Rest accurate.

physical_harm.quote: as many as 8 injuries were noted on the body of the deceased

number_of_offences.reason: Five charged; conviction on s.302 with 148/149.

motive.quote: due to old enmity, attacked with sharp weapon with intention to kill

key_evidence_accepted.quote: fully supported by the version of P.W.6, and also fully corroborated by the evidence of P.Ws. 7 and 11

witness_credibility.quote: evidence of P.W.3 as an eye witness was cogent in every respect

trial_duration.quote: Division Bench of the High Court... dated 7th September, 2006
trial_duration.reason: Dates are accurate; trial date not given.

legal_representation.quote: Tripurari Ray, Dhirendra Singh Parmar, Suresh Kumar Sharma

investigation_status.quote: arrest of the appellants effected on 28th June, 1997 and the subsequent seizure made on 29th June, 1997

procedural_irregularity.quote: even assuming the delay did really happen in forwarding the Express Report, we find that such a delay has not caused any serious prejudice

appeal_history.quote: The Division Bench having confirmed the conviction and sentence

prosecution_argument.quote: the arrest of the accused and the seizure made by the panch witnesses duly established that the appellants were involved

defence_argument.quote: the FIR was ante-dated and that the appellants were falsely implicated

legal_principle_applied.quote: Every such delay is not fatal unless prejudice to the accused is shown

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Pala Singh v. State of Punjab (1972) 2 SCC 640
